Here are **5 easy-level LeetCode tree questions** that are great for practice (especially if you’re revising for interviews or a lab test):  

---

1. **[LeetCode 94 – Binary Tree Inorder Traversal](https://leetcode.com/problems/binary-tree-inorder-traversal/)**  
   👉 *Concepts:* Recursion, Stack  
   - Given the root of a binary tree, return its inorder traversal.  
   - Focus on recursion or iterative stack-based traversal.

---

2. **[LeetCode 104 – Maximum Depth of Binary Tree](https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-depth-of-binary-tree/)**  
   👉 *Concepts:* Recursion, DFS, BFS  
   - Find how deep the tree goes.  
   - Classic beginner problem to learn how recursion works on trees.

---

3. **[LeetCode 100 – Same Tree](https://leetcode.com/problems/same-tree/)**  
   👉 *Concepts:* Recursion, Comparison  
   - Check if two binary trees are identical (same structure + same values).  
   - Teaches basic recursive comparison.

---

4. **[LeetCode 226 – Invert Binary Tree](https://leetcode.com/problems/invert-binary-tree/)**  
   👉 *Concepts:* Recursion, DFS  
   - Swap left and right subtrees recursively.  
   - One of the most common tree interview problems.

---

5. **[LeetCode 112 – Path Sum](https://leetcode.com/problems/path-sum/)**  
   👉 *Concepts:* Recursion, DFS  
   - Check if the tree has a root-to-leaf path that adds up to a given target sum.  
   - Great for learning how to carry values through recursive calls.

---

Perfect — let’s talk **Linked List easy-level LeetCode questions** 👇  

These are the go-to problems you’ll see early in interviews or labs.  

---

### 🧩 **Top 5 Easy Linked List Problems on LeetCode**

1. **[LeetCode 206 – Reverse Linked List](https://leetcode.com/problems/reverse-linked-list/)**  
   👉 *Concepts:* Iteration, Pointer manipulation  
   - Reverse a singly linked list.  
   - Most classic linked list problem ever.  
   - Teaches how to rewire `next` pointers safely.

---

2. **[LeetCode 141 – Linked List Cycle](https://leetcode.com/problems/linked-list-cycle/)**  
   👉 *Concepts:* Floyd’s Tortoise and Hare (two-pointer)  
   - Detect if there’s a cycle in a linked list.  
   - Introduces slow and fast pointer technique.

---

3. **[LeetCode 21 – Merge Two Sorted Lists](https://leetcode.com/problems/merge-two-sorted-lists/)**  
   👉 *Concepts:* Two-pointer, Recursion  
   - Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list.  
   - Great for learning list construction and dummy nodes.

---

4. **[LeetCode 83 – Remove Duplicates from Sorted List](https://leetcode.com/problems/remove-duplicates-from-sorted-list/)**  
   👉 *Concepts:* Simple traversal  
   - Given a *sorted* list, delete all duplicates.  
   - Straightforward pointer move problem.

---

5. **[LeetCode 876 – Middle of the Linked List](https://leetcode.com/problems/middle-of-the-linked-list/)**  
   👉 *Concepts:* Slow and fast pointer  
   - Return the middle node of a linked list.  
   - Clean and short, very common test question.

---
